Sarah Scully   11:21 AM
Thanks, Morgan. Great. Ciara from my team will go ahead and book that in. Looking forward to connecting next week.




                                      Meeting Ideas


1. Custom Workflows for Encrypted Messaging + Payment Flows
What’s the challenge?
Hopscotch currently allows users to create deals inside a chat — which is great for simplicity and user adoption. But as they grow, users will demand more flexibility:
What if I’m buying a service, not a product?


What if the deal needs to happen in stages (e.g. 50% payment now, 50% later)?


What if the verifier needs to approve something before payment moves?


Right now, they likely have hardcoded flows or basic templates. That won’t scale.
What you’re proposing:
A customizable transaction engine that sits underneath the chat UI but lets Hopscotch create different deal flows depending on context.
Examples:
Milestone-Based Payments: Ideal for services like freelance work. Each milestone triggers a partial release from escrow, verified by either party or a third party.


Auto-Escrow Expiry: Funds automatically return to buyer if the deal isn’t confirmed in X hours/days.


Conditional Verifier Logic: For example, a deal can’t be finalized unless a verifier gives a green light.


Multi-Sig Style Approvals: If multiple verifiers are involved, all must agree before funds are released.


Why it’s useful to them:
This gives Hopscotch the ability to grow horizontally into new use cases — services, rentals, bookings, time-based agreements — without changing the core UX. Everything still happens inside a chat, but with more powerful logic driving the transaction under the hood.

2. Visual Admin Layer for Deal Integrity + Risk Monitoring
What’s the challenge?
Hopscotch is built to be light-touch, low-overhead. That’s great — until volume scales and things start breaking. Without the right visibility tools, they won’t know:
Which deals are failing?


Which users or verifiers are creating bad experiences?


Is a certain community seeing more disputes?


Is someone gaming the system?


Right now, they likely see basic logs or backend events. That’s not enough to manage risk or improve UX at scale.
What you’re proposing:
A dashboard for internal visibility — not for users, but for the Hopscotch team to monitor protocol health and surface key signals.
Features it could include:
Deal Activity Map: See active deals, statuses (pending, disputed, resolved), and total value transacted.


Risk Flags: Auto-flag deals that are delayed, disputed, or involve repeat problematic wallets.


Verifier Insights: Track verifier performance — how often they’re used, how often their decisions are disputed, etc.


Escrow Anomalies: Spot wallets with unusually high transaction volume or behavior that suggests fraud or laundering.


Dispute Heatmaps: Visualize patterns over time — are disputes spiking after certain product updates?


Why it’s useful to them:
This helps them:
Catch risk signals early


Maintain a high-trust reputation


Feed data into future product decisions (e.g. verifier incentives, smart defaults)


Eventually support protocol governance if they decentralize part of the verifier ecosystem



3. Optional: SDK/API Toolkit for External Communities Using Deal Frames
(Only bring this up if it feels relevant during the call — e.g. if Morgan mentions growing the Deal Frames or working with external partners.)
What’s the challenge?
Hopscotch wants to be infrastructure, not just an app. They’re already letting people embed deals into social feeds via Deal Frames. But what if:
A Discord server wants custom deal rules for its members?


A Farcaster community wants every deal to include one of their own verifiers?


A vertical marketplace (e.g. rare books or coaching) wants to predefine deal templates?


Right now, they’d need dev resources to integrate those variations. That slows growth.
What you’re proposing:
An API/SDK toolkit or even a no-code portal that communities can use to:
Set up their own verifier rules


Predefine escrow logic (e.g. how long funds stay locked, who resolves disputes)


Add custom branding or deal templates


Get analytics on their deal activity


Why it’s useful to them:
This makes Hopscotch instantly plug-and-play for communities — DAOs, Discords, niche marketplaces — without burdening Hopscotch’s dev team. It also grows the deal volume without growing operational cost.

How to Tie It All Together on the Call:
Start by saying something like:
"Morgan, I know you're focused on scaling trust without growing complexity — especially with how users interact through messaging. Based on your model, I see a few key ways we could help Hopscotch move faster without adding bulk to your core team."
Then walk them through the 2 main ideas:
Custom deal workflows inside chat


Internal deal intelligence layer


Optionally: mention the SDK idea if it fits.
Then close with something like:
"We’re not here to rebuild what you’ve already got. This is about accelerating where you're already headed — more flexible, more scalable, without compromising on trust or simplicity."

Curious—are more of your partners asking for digital support around asset monitoring and seabed data modeling, or is your team mostly focused on the mechanical side of innovation?

Just want to give you a quick idea of what I’d love to discuss: How a custom software development company can help you. Here are a few ideas off the top of my head: real-time data dashboards for anchor stress/load, internal systems to track project timelines, and lightweight apps for crew to log drilling reports from sea.

Just wanted to follow up on my earlier message, really intrigued by the work Subsea Micropiles is doing in robotic seabed drilling and marine anchor systems.

                                                           Meeting Ideas

1. Real-Time Anchor Stress/Load Dashboard
What it does:
It’s a live, browser-based dashboard that shows the stress/load on each installed micropile or mooring anchor in real time.
How it works:
Load cells or strain gauges are embedded during or after installation.


Data from these sensors is transmitted (wired or wireless) to a local unit onboard the vessel or platform.


That data is sent (when in range) to a centralized cloud system.


Your team and the client can log in and monitor:


Live anchor load (in kN or MPa)


Historical stress curves per pile


Alerts if any anchor exceeds safe thresholds


Why this matters for Mark:
Subsea Micropiles is proving that smaller, robotic-installed piles can handle serious loads. A real-time stress dashboard makes that transparent and verifiable:
Reduces risk of structural failure


Helps with regulatory compliance


Builds trust with clients in offshore wind or oil & gas, who demand reliability


Can be shown during commissioning or audits to demonstrate pile integrity



2. Seabed Data Modeling and Visualization Platform
What it does:
Turns raw geotechnical and bathymetric data into a clear, interactive 3D model of the seabed and subsurface conditions.
How it works:
You upload seabed data from surveys (e.g., CPT logs, boreholes, side-scan sonar).


The platform interpolates gaps, builds a layered map showing soil types, depths, slopes.


You can overlay:


Planned micropile locations


Environmental exclusion zones


Cable or pipeline routing


Why this matters for Mark:
Micropiles work in varied geology. This tool:
Helps project engineers plan more precisely


Makes seabed risk visual and easy to communicate (internally or to clients)


Can be used pre-bid to assess viability or show competence


Becomes part of handover deliverables to wind farm developers, etc.



3. Lightweight Field Logging App for Drilling Crews
What it does:
An offline-capable mobile app used by crew to log every pile installation directly from the vessel.
Key fields:
Pile ID


Location (auto GPS)


Start/End time


Drill depth


Soil type


Torque/load readings


Cement volume used


Any issues (washout, refusal, kickback)


Extra features:
Photo upload


Signature capture


Syncs with cloud when back online


Daily logs auto-compiled for PM review


Why this matters for Mark:
Right now, a lot of this probably lives in Excel or handwritten logs. This app:
Cuts admin time for crew


Standardizes data across teams/projects


Feeds into reports and dashboards automatically


Reduces communication lag between offshore and HQ



4. Internal Project Timeline Tracker
What it does:
Tracks the full lifecycle of each offshore project—from design and mobilization to execution and handover.
Features:
Kanban-style view of each stage (e.g., seabed survey, design freeze, transport, install, QA)


Linked to milestones (e.g., “First pile installed” or “50% complete”)


Shared visibility for PMs, engineering, ops


Why this matters for Mark:
They’re scaling up with multiple vessels, a new Scotland facility, and large anchor deployments. This gives:
Visibility across sites and teams


Less back-and-forth email tracking


A high-level view for leadership, with drill-down for ops



5. Asset Monitoring System
What it does:
Tracks condition and usage of critical equipment like:
Robotic drills


Mixing systems


Power units


Anchor frames


Each asset has:
Serial number


Location


Last used


Maintenance log


Assigned project


Why this matters:
They’ve invested €10M+ into R&D and robotic drilling. This system:
Protects that investment


Prevents delays from failed equipment


Supports ISO/process audits


Reduces unplanned downtime from maintenance gaps



6. Digital Commissioning + Inspection Logs
What it does:
Gives field teams a checklist-based app for final anchor inspections.
Checklist items might include:
Anchor fully embedded


Load test passed (values recorded)


Tension verified


Photo documentation complete


Signature from field lead


Auto-generates:
A commissioning certificate (PDF)


Status dashboard (complete / pending / flagged)


Why this matters for Mark:
Offshore clients want evidence. This gives a verifiable, timestamped trail of every step taken—without extra work.

7. Auto-Generated Drill Reports
What it does:
Compiles all data from field logs, sensors, and project timelines into a polished, client-facing report.
Includes:
Summary table of all piles installed


Performance data (drill time, torque, cement, etc.)


Deviations/issues flagged


Maps or visuals


Final inspection sign-offs


Auto-generated every day or week, depending on need.
Why this matters:
Clients like floating wind developers or oil majors expect this. But generating it manually is a huge time suck. This saves hours, improves accuracy, and helps closeout faster.

8. Predictive Load + Maintenance Insights
What it does:
Analyzes long-term stress/load data across installations to predict when anchors might need inspection, retensioning, or replacement.
Uses:
Load trends


Environmental data (storms, currents)


Pile type and soil profile


Machine learning or rules-based logic flags anomalies.
Why this matters:
Right now, inspections are scheduled manually or reactively. This shifts to condition-based maintenance—making Subsea Micropiles look even smarter and more forward-thinking than their competitors.

Summary (to use with Mark on the call)
Mark, you're already doing some of the most innovative work in offshore anchoring with your robotic micropiling. What we're proposing isn't reinventing what you do, it's capturing and amplifying it. These tools are designed to make your installations smarter, your data more useful, and your reporting faster and clearer. Whether it's for internal control, client trust, or scaling to new geos, they slot in right where the real complexity is offshore, in the field, and under pressure.

1. Repair-Readiness Predictor
The Problem Now
 EasyStall only knows whether an item can be resold after it’s unpacked and inspected in the warehouse. That means:
Every return gets the same initial handling, whether it’s a broken item or something in perfect condition


Valuable, quick-turn items wait in the same queue as low-value, high-repair ones


You can’t forecast resale stock in advance to update clients or push to marketplaces


The Idea
 We build a tool that pulls live data from carriers and return portals (via APIs). This data includes:
Return reason codes (“wrong size”, “damaged”, “defective”)


Carrier scan notes (“box damaged”, “contents shifted”)


Delivery/return timelines (longer trips = higher damage risk)


Product SKU and past return history


The system uses this data to score each incoming return before it arrives—basically saying:
“90% likely to be resale-ready”


“Medium probability – inspect for repair”


“Low probability – route to recycling”


The Payoff
Prioritization: High-probability resale items skip the wait and hit the inspection bench first


Forecasting: You can tell clients in advance “We expect X units resale-ready by tomorrow”


Warehouse efficiency: You avoid handling items twice



2. AI-Powered Condition Grading
The Problem Now
 Condition checks are manual. That means time, subjective judgment, and the risk of inconsistency.
The Idea
 When an item is unpacked at intake, your team already takes photos (or could with little change). We plug those images into an AI vision model trained for:
Cosmetic defects (scratches, dents, tears, stains)


Packaging state (sealed, open, damaged)


Signs of use (worn soles, missing tags, faded color)


Missing components (empty slots in product trays)


It instantly outputs a condition grade—for example:
Grade A: Resell immediately


Grade B: Send to light repair/refurb


Grade C: Scrap or recycle


The grading ties directly into your Returnless dashboard so the client sees the result in real time.
The Payoff
Inspection time per item drops sharply


Fewer misroutes (a slightly damaged but valuable product doesn’t get wrongly scrapped)


Your “6x faster processing” claim gets even stronger



3. Intelligent Workflow Routing
The Problem Now
 Even with your current dashboard, most routing is still human-triggered. That’s time and mental load for your staff.
The Idea
 We merge the Repair-Readiness Predictor + AI Grading into a single rules engine. As soon as an item’s predicted state and actual grade are in, the system:
Auto-assigns it to the right physical area in the warehouse (repair bench, refurb line, resale shelf, recycling zone)


Updates the client dashboard instantly with a meaningful status (“repair in progress – ready by Friday”)


Pushes resale-ready items to marketplaces or back to client inventory systems without waiting for a manual push


The Payoff
Consistent decision-making with almost zero manual clicks


Clients see useful updates, not just “in progress”


Faster turnaround = higher resale rate



How to frame it on the call
 You don’t dump all of this at once. You start with what EasyStall already does well, then ask a question that makes the gap obvious:
“Davey, you’ve already nailed the physical side of returns. But how much visibility do you have on resale-ready stock before it arrives? And how consistent is grading between team members?”
Then you walk him through:
Prediction before arrival


Instant grading at intake


Automated routing + dashboard updates

Description:
Hi,

I am hoping to build order shipping software/platform like Eshopworld or Shipstation. I am making exploratory investigations into how much this is going to cost and don't know exactly everything that is needed to build such a platform. I do know I will need integrate logistics carriers API's into my platform for shipping times and rates and am hoping to using World Options for this although I am open to using other firms. 

I will also need to build in a payments side (exchange rates, customs, excise, VAT calculations, shipping, percentage to be taken by my company out of each transaction) of the platform and am hoping to use Stripe to do this however I am open to learning if this is the best option and if it can be done without their help. 

I would prefer if you contacted me via email and discussed if it would be possible to build such software and give a rough estimate on how much this might cost in total. If I decide to go with your company we can then discuss the ins and outs and details of building the platform.

Project Background:
I wanted to ship Gap clothes to Ireland from America and they didn’t ship here. Nautica, Dockers and other brands ship to some countries but not all countries and that includes Ireland. I reflected on this to see if this was a problem I could solve and started down this road. I did research and came across an Irish (I am Irish) order shipping software company. Of course, I recognised this company as they do the order shipping software for one of my favourite American brands J-Crew. The name of the company is eShopWorld. I am still putting all the pieces together and learning as I go and I still do not have a full idea of all the pieces required for my software/platform but I have a few calls set up for the new year when someone who is in this exact business will walk me through what is required to build such a software.
The Problem:
The problem I identified is that there are many e-commerce marketplaces and sellers who do not ship to certain countries.
The Solution:
I aim to solve this problem by providing a plug and play e-commerce platform/software to individual vendor businesses that will enable them to ship internationally and to otherwise unreachable countries. It will be code inserted on top of vendor website code and will manage and complete everything related to orders and delivery.
Platforms: 
Web initially but as it’s a plug and play software that inserts on top of the vendor websites code, it will be mainly for website vendors.
Main set of features/Functionality:
Four main products - starter, basic, intermediate & advanced for different quantities of orders the vendor websites/clients will be receiving and fulfilling. Some of the subject areas around order shipping include add-on advanced features for the software: compliance, data analytics, fraud protection, risk management, supplier relationship management and demand generation.
Furthermore, the software will include the following services: Import orders from 100+ selling channels, marketplaces, Enterprise Resource Planning, Customer Relationship Management, or Inventory Management Software which includes the ability to do scan-based workflows, bulk updates, and automation processes to quickly fulfil the day’s shipments.
Functionalities: 
Payments - everything payments related - so hoping to work with Stripe for this part if your firm doesn’t deal with payments. This will include calculating exchange rates on orders, customs, excise, VAT, shipping rates and selling price for the goods in question. 
Order fulfilment: Once the payment is made the order has to be fulfilled. This requires physical packaging of the goods and collection by logistics carrier. It will entail a system which will track and trace every order from payment to delivery.
Logistics - for this we will be using a logistics carrier company like World Options (these are firms that have multiple logistics companies like FedEx and DHL in their offerings so that goods can be booked on shipments and moved) and plugging their APIs into our software so that shipping times & rates will be calculated when taking and receiving the order.
Seller channels - What online marketplace my e-commerce prospects sell on e.g. seller fulfilled Prime, EBay etc. This I have to find out about from the person I have the call with a person who is in this exact business. In short, he will tell me how to advertise or plug-in the platform to sellers on marketplaces like Amazon 
Warehouse/Inventory Management. For more advanced users who have large companies or brands shipping large quantities of goods in short space of time. Establish efficient storage and digital inventory management systems. Inventory Management Systems (IMS) are digital tools that enable real-time tracking and management of inventory. Key components often include barcoding systems, RFID technology, software platforms, and analytics. Most of the customers have their own fulfilment operation but they advertise on Amazon and fulfil directly. They help sellers reach different market places. As I’m unsure whether the carrier logistics firms carry out this side of the business, I am unsure if this will be required.
Features/Functionality:
Client User Interface:
Order Management: This will include an interactive interface where clients can manage and edit orders. Details on functionalities and dropdown choices for each order. Create New Order, View Orders, Edit Order, Cancel Order, Order Status, Order History, Shipping Information, Invoice/Receipt, Returns and Refunds, Payment Information, Customer Communication, Fulfillment Details, Batch Processing, Export Orders, Archive Orders, Settings and Configuration, Help and Support:
Shipping Management: This will include interactive interface where clients can manage and edit shipping arrangements. Details on functionalities and dropdown choices for each order. supply chain visibility and tracking. The wealth of data collected through IoT sensors, RFID, and GPS tracking can be analysed to identify trends and areas for improvement in the supply chain. This data-driven approach can lead to more efficient operations and cost savings
Inventory Management: This will include interactive interface where clients can manage and edit their own inventory. Details on functionalities and dropdown choices for each order. Inventory Management Systems (IMS) are digital tools that enable real-time tracking and management of inventory. Key components often include barcoding systems, RFID technology, software platforms, and analytics. The benefits for clients include efficient order fulfilment. Clients benefit from rapid, accurate, and efficient order processing, ensuring that products are shipped promptly and accurately. Clients have real-time visibility into their inventory levels, helping them avoid overstocking or stockouts, and make informed decisions about restocking.
Returns Management: To structure a fee that covers returns of goods in an e-commerce business, you can implement a returns policy that includes the following elements: 1.) Return Window: Define a specific period within which customers can request returns, such as 30 days from the date of purchase. 2.) Return Eligibility: Clearly outline the conditions under which returns are accepted. This may include criteria such as unused or unopened items, original packaging, and proof of purchase. 3.) Return Authorization: Require customers to request authorization for returns through your website or customer support channels. This allows you to track and approve returns. 4.) Return Shipping: Specify who is responsible for return shipping costs. Options include: Free returns: The e-commerce business covers return shipping costs. Customer-paid returns: Customers are responsible for return shipping fees. Split returns: Both the business and the customer share the return shipping costs. 5.) Restocking Fees: Consider implementing a restocking fee for returns to cover handling and processing expenses. This fee can be a fixed amount or a percentage of the item's purchase price. 6.) Refund Methods: Clearly communicate how refunds will be processed. Options include: Full refund to the original payment method. Store credit or gift card for future purchases. Exchange for a different product. 7.) Return Process: Provide step-by-step instructions for customers on how to initiate a return, including where to send the item and any required documentation. 8.) Return Tracking: Implement a system to track returns and refunds to ensure a smooth process and prevent fraud. 9.) Transparency: Make your return policy easy to find on your website and ensure it's written in clear, understandable language. 10.) Customer Support: Offer responsive customer support to assist customers with return inquiries and provide timely updates on the status of their returns.
Compliance, Data Security, Fraud Protection – 1.) Regulatory Compliance: Overview of compliance standards and certifications achieved by the platform, such as GDPR, PCI DSS, HIPAA, etc. Access to compliance documentation and reports for auditing purposes. 2.) Data Encryption: Option to enable encryption for data in transit and at rest to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access. Choice of encryption algorithms and key management. 3.) User Access Control: User role management to assign specific access privileges based on job roles and responsibilities. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) for an added layer of user security. 4.) Data Privacy Settings: Configuration options for data privacy settings, allowing clients to define data retention policies and consent management.5.) Audit Logs: Access to detailed logs of user activities, data access, and system events for compliance auditing. Ability to search and filter audit logs for specific events or time periods. 6.) Compliance Reporting: Generation of compliance reports that clients can use for internal and external audits or regulatory submissions. 7.) Data Masking and Redaction: Features to mask or redact sensitive data in user interfaces, reports, or exports to maintain data privacy. 8.) Secure File Upload/Download: Secure methods for clients to upload and download sensitive documents or data files. Scanning and malware detection for uploaded files. 9.) Fraud Detection and Prevention: Real-time monitoring for suspicious activities and transactions. Integration with fraud detection algorithms and third-party services. 10.) Authentication and Authorization: Management of user authentication methods, password policies, and access control rules. Role-based access control (RBAC) to define permissions for different user roles. 11.) Compliance Training and Resources: Access to compliance training materials, guidelines, and resources to educate clients on best practices. Notifications for compliance updates and changes in regulations. 12.) Incident Response Plan: Information about the platform's incident response plan, including how security incidents are reported and managed. 13.) Data Backups and Disaster Recovery: Information about data backup processes and disaster recovery plans to ensure data availability and continuity. 14.) Security Notifications: Alerts and notifications related to security threats, breaches, or vulnerabilities that may affect the client's data or operations. 15.) Compliance Assistance: Contact information for compliance support and assistance, including dedicated compliance teams or consultants. 16.) Third-Party Audits and Certifications: Details about third-party audits and certifications obtained by the platform, along with associated documentation. 17.) Compliance Dashboard: An interactive dashboard providing an overview of compliance status, security metrics, and any outstanding compliance tasks. 
Automated Payment Reconciliation & Performance Metrics: Eshopworld employs automated payment reconciliation processes, ensuring accurate and efficient matching of payments with orders and reducing manual effort. It will also show graphs of performance metrics to analysie performance and enhance ways to improve service to clients customers.
Data Feedback Loop/Customer Service: Including “about” the firm, office address, email and send message portal.
Account Management/Settings: Account User information. Subscription Billing Services: For recurring payments or subscription-based models, Eshopworld may provide subscription billing services, automating the billing process for merchants.
********************************************************************************
Customer User Interface (On Vendor Websites):
IP Address Detection on entry to website: Once country is detected customised exchange language and pricing of products is adapted to country of customer origin. 
Customisable Checkout: Clients will be able to design a checkout on their website with code that inserts on top of the vendor website code. Automatically calculate local currency, payment options, customs, excise, VAT Shipping cost and selling price into total cost to customer. Options include quantity of products they are selling, price breakdown and total, product number, order number generation, receipt, and email confirmation generation. Payments, Localised Pricing, Duty, Tax, Language, & Currency

*******************************************************************************
Optional Client User Interface Add-ons depending on the price for Developer to build them:
Data Analytics/Predictive Insights: Implement advanced analytics tools and machine learning algorithms to derive predictive insights for improved decision-making. Data Analytics and Predictive Insights involve the use of advanced analytics tools, data mining, and machine learning algorithms to analyze large datasets and derive valuable insights. By integrating these capabilities into the e-commerce platform, Import/Export Point can make data-driven decisions, such as demand forecasting and pricing optimization, ultimately enhancing the client experience. These tools encompass data analysis, statistical modeling, and predictive analytics to extract meaningful insights from data. Machine learning algorithms can be applied for various purposes, such as demand prediction, route optimization, and customer behavior analysis
Demand Generation – Demand Forecasting: Use demand forecasting models and algorithms to predict stock requirements and automate replenishment. Demand Forecasting and Inventory Replenishment involve the application of data-driven models and algorithms to predict product demand and ensure optimal stock levels. By integrating these systems into the e-commerce platform, vendors can maintain the right amount of inventory, reducing the risk of stockouts and overstocking. These models analyze historical sales data, market trends, and external factors to predict future demand for specific products. Replenishment algorithms use demand forecasts to automatically generate orders for restocking products that are running low.
Risk Management and Contingency Planning. Develop risk assessment models and contingency plans to address potential disruptions. Risk Management and Contingency Planning focus on identifying potential disruptions in the supply chain and developing strategies to mitigate their impact. The integration of these strategies into the e-commerce platform ensures that clients can rely on a resilient logistics system. These measures help reduce the risk of delays and uncertainties. Risk Assessment Models: These models evaluate potential risks and vulnerabilities in the supply chain, such as natural disasters, labor strikes, or customs issues. Contingency Plans: Plans outline how to respond to identified risks and include strategies for alternative routing, resource allocation, and communication.
Supplier Relationship Management (SRM). Establish Supplier Relationship Management systems to optimize interactions with logistics partners. Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) involves the establishment of systems and practices to enhance interactions and collaboration with logistics partners, such as carriers, warehouses, and service providers. By integrating SRM into the e-commerce platform, Import/Export Point can improve the reliability and service quality of its logistics network. Supplier Collaboration Tools: These tools facilitate communication, data sharing, and collaboration with logistics partners. Performance Monitoring and KPIs: SRM systems often include key performance indicators (KPIs) to track and evaluate the performance of logistics partners.
Incoterms Implementation: Eshopworld implements appropriate Incoterms in transactions, clearly defining the responsibilities of buyers and sellers regarding shipping, customs, and payment.

Hey Anna,

To respect your time, I’ll be straightforward: I’m reaching out because I believe what we do could align with Connected Childhood’s work in evidence-based parenting and child-focused education.

Since Connected Childhood is helping families and professionals build emotional resilience, skill, and calm through accessible expert-led programs, I thought of two ways to strengthen that:

A custom learning portal to host self-paced courses and track user progress across parenting and CPD modules

Mobile-friendly tools for parents to access bite-sized mindfulness and play therapy practices on the go

Sharing our work here: https://squareroot.ie/portfolio, it speaks louder than anything I can write.

As a custom software development company, we usually come in when teams are ready to invest in what’s next & need external support to move faster without stretching internal resources.

Would you be open to a quick 15-minute call either this week or next week to discuss whether this aligns with your plans? Or are you still in the early stages of exploring what to build next?

Our Web And App Development Portfolio | Square Root Solutions
squareroot.ie

Hi Anna,

Just wanted to follow up on my earlier message about potential ways to support Connected Childhood, specifically the idea of a custom learning portal for your courses and mobile-friendly tools for busy parents.

I know how much thought goes into building something that helps families, so if you’re starting to think about what’s next or need external dev support, I’d love to connect.

Would a quick 15-minute call sometime this or next week work for you?

Anna McGrath (She/Her)  9:18 PM

Sarah Scully   11:06 AM
Hi Anna,

That's perfect, Wednesday at 10:30. Could you please share your best email address so that Ciara from my team can send the meeting invite?

Looking forward to our chat!


Anna McGrath (She/Her)  1:09 PM
Yes, it’s info@connectedchildhood.com




Sarah Scully   1:11 PM
Thank you. Ciara will send through the calendar invite for Wednesday at 10:30.

Looking forward to connecting then!




                                  Meeting Ideas

📞 Suggested Call Flow
1. Warm Intro (2 mins)
Thank Anna for her time.


Acknowledge Connected Childhood’s impact: “I love how you’re blending play therapy, mindfulness, and education — it’s rare to see such a holistic approach.”


Transition: “When I read about your programmes and the upcoming subscription, it struck me that technology could really help scale your reach while keeping the personal, calm touch you’re known for.”



2. Reframe the Conversation (2–3 mins)
Confirm their direction: “From what I understand, Connected Childhood is building structured learning journeys — like the Discovery Programme and future subscription model — and at the same time, you want families to have easy, ongoing access to your resources.”


Then: “We thought of two ways software could help support those goals.”



3. Idea #1 – Custom Learning Portal (5 mins)
🔹 What it is: A secure, branded platform where all courses, consultations, and community resources live in one place.
🔹 How it works
Programme Delivery: The Discovery Programme could be hosted with videos, guided practices, and live Q&A all within one structured flow. Parents wouldn’t need scattered links/emails.


Masterclasses & Consultations: Parents book, watch, and follow up all from the same dashboard. The 10-minute follow-up calls could be auto-scheduled after course completion.


Certificates for CPD: For teacher and professional users, the system could generate CPD certificates automatically, adding credibility to Connected Childhood’s training.


Community & Subscription: As you roll out your monthly subscription, members could unlock ongoing resources, join live group calls, and access a parent discussion forum.


🔹 Why this matters for Connected Childhood
Keeps the experience professional & seamless (parents feel like they’re part of a structured programme).


Reduces admin time for you — no chasing emails, links, or follow-ups manually.


Scales your reach — once set up, you can deliver the Discovery Programme to 20 parents or 200 parents without stretching your team.


Example to share on call:
“Instead of parents juggling Zoom links, PDFs, and email reminders, everything is in one place. They log in, see their progress, get reminders, and even earn certificates. It turns Connected Childhood into a real online hub — not just a series of disconnected sessions.”

4. Idea #2 – Mobile-Friendly Parenting Companion App (5 mins)
🔹 What it is: A supportive app for busy parents, giving them on-the-go access to Connected Childhood practices and resources.
🔹 How it works
Quick Tools for Stressful Moments: A parent dealing with bedtime meltdowns could open the app and play a 3-minute mindfulness or play activity.


Daily Nudges: Notifications like “Take 2 minutes of calm before school drop-off” to encourage consistent practice.


Personalized Content: If someone finished a Masterclass on “Managing Overwhelm,” the app suggests related practices for the week.


Offline Mode: Resources available even without WiFi — perfect for school runs, waiting rooms, or late evenings.


🔹 Why this matters for Connected Childhood
Extends the real-life application of what you teach. Parents don’t just learn — they practice in the moment.


Increases engagement and retention — the more parents use Connected Childhood daily, the more likely they’ll continue into subscriptions.


Strengthens emotional connection — the app feels like Connected Childhood is “right there in their pocket.”


Example to share on call:
“Imagine a mum who just completed your Discovery Programme. She’s had a tough morning with her child. Instead of trying to remember what she learned in a video weeks ago, she opens the app and gets a 2-minute grounding exercise. That’s the kind of everyday support that builds loyalty and real impact.”

5. Optional Extension – Insights & Growth (2–3 mins)
With both the portal & app, Connected Childhood could see what parents engage with most.


Example insights:


Which masterclasses parents finish vs. drop off.


Which mindfulness practices get repeated the most.


Data that shows real-world impact — useful for funding, partnerships, or schools.



6. Wrap-Up & Next Steps (3–4 mins)
Transition into a question: “Does this align with what you’re planning for Connected Childhood in the next 6–12 months?”


Based on her answer:


If she’s interested → suggest a follow-up discovery session where your team maps out her digital roadmap.


If she’s hesitant → ask, “What’s the most pressing area for you — course delivery, parent engagement, or scaling subscriptions?”



✅ In summary, your call narrative should:
Recognize her work (empathy & alignment).


Show you understand her business model.


Present two clear, logical, relevant solutions (portal + app).


Leave space for her to respond with what’s most important.

Captions that can be edited in real time by the teacher or parent


Preset difficulty levels that adapt language complexity to the child’s reading ability

Hello Pavle,

I read about your perspective on Tesla's quote and the intriguing connection to quantum consciousness—fascinating! As science continues to explore these ideas, what recent discoveries or correlations do you find most compelling in this area?


Pavle Kostić  6:17 PM
Hey Sarah! Glad to be connected.

One of the interesting correlations is that this year Nobel laureate John Hopfield put foundation to modern AI through so called Hopfield Neural Networks which in turn are based on same physical and mathematical principles like Cellular Neural Networks (invented by prof. Leon O. Chua). These principles, which are basically driving the ’intelligence’ of these systems are based on principles of energy optimizations, described through Lyapunov functions. While Hopfield’s Networks established correlation between energy optimization and intelligence, they were ’artificial’ in sense that their topology was not realistic for biological systems – they had every neuron connected to every other, which is impractical in real-world and biological systems where we know that each neuron is connected only to some neighbors not to every other one in the brain. There is where Cellular Neural Networks fill the gap as they are topological structures where neurons are connected in local neighborhoods, aligning well with biological structures we see. I researched extensively Cellular Neural networks and even developed few original models and systems which were exhibiting not only intelligent but even cognitive properties. And these exactly cognitive properties of functionalities of these neural networks (I named them Fractal-Modular networks) have some mathematical properties that are now found in Quantum systems and computers.

Now back to Tesla’s quote – if you connect the dots from above and if you recall that Universe is basically (based on laws of physics) just an huge energy optimization ‘mechanism’, I hope you will find it intriguing to ask a questions: if Universe is ‘intelligent’ in Hopfield’s sense? And if it is intelligent, is it also consciousness?

Personally, I’m really excited to see that quantum computing progress is enabling the creation of new cognitive system, symbiosis with Fractal-Modular i.e. Cellular i.e. Hopfield’s Neural Networks, opening practical possibility to build much advanced and potentially ways more powerful ‘intelligence’ than current top-notch AI systems based on massive but legacy computing (electrical) technology.

Thanks for sharing, Pavle! This is absolutely fascinating—especially how the evolution from Hopfield to Cellular Neural Networks aligns with biological systems and even quantum properties.

The connection you made to Tesla’s quote is intriguing. The idea of the universe as an energy optimization "mechanism" sparks so many questions. If it’s "intelligent" in Hopfield’s sense, could quantum computing eventually model or even interact with this universal "consciousness"?

I’d love to hear more about your thoughts on how these advancements might shape AI systems and, more broadly, our understanding of intelligence itself!

Hi Sarah! This is a very deep and intriguing question. It is not easy to answer it shortly and not to sound profound.

 I may just share with you a bit of clue: while very recently you may find Western researchers talking about and publishing scientific papers and research on quantum effects in the brain, I have learned about it 30 years ago at University. I had a professor who studied in Moscow (while it was still the USSR) and there Russians for 50+ years researched the quantum fenomena in the brain and their effects on our sensations and 'shaping of reality' like time reversal and time-space bending in Einstein's sense. I would not fare to say I become expert by listening one semester of this but I can say I learned enough to understand the concepts and (as we never had adequate equipment and labs for that kind of research) to try to apply some bits and pieces in neural networks we could research much more easily.

So you may connect the dots. As there is more and more evidence or at least indications of quantum effects are not only present but driving important cognitive processes in the brain, it also gives at least 'technical compatibility' with universal 'consciousness'.

This allows for fundamentally novel approaches not only for easy to imagine practical products for augmentation of brain functionalities.

But commercial and practical improvements of individual brain is very probably exactly what quantum is all about - collectivism instead of individualism. Quantum entanglement is collectivism as it ties particles making them new collective entity rather the group of individuals.

So my expectation is that quantum interfacing should enable fully new way we engage human brains and make us more engaged into collaborative cognition among ourselves but potentially with other beings out there. Hi Sarah,
I would say, not without a certain sense of this being an old UX adage - it depends. I think that the spread between consideration of UX from the very beginning and integrating it with a live app should be tackled based on company size, its investment capabilities, and project management trajectory.

 However, as time goes on, and UX becomes more prevalent - the slow increase of UX inclusion should be visible for all companies. Basically, as industry grows and refines products, so does their UX maturity improve on average.

 And lastly, basically the split, in my experience remains stable. Some companies just can afford it early, and do so, some need  to learn the hard way, others are lucky enough to have versatile enough team to succeed despite that, but never exclude possibility for the future, more focused UX improvements.(Edited)
